summary: Enable self-service Jira/Confluence/Slack project bootstrap with policy guardrails
description: Request: Build a self-service workflow so product and platform pods can create a pre-approved combination of Jira project, Confluence space, and Slack channel via a single portal action. Rationale: current provisioning is manual, high-touch, and inconsistent — teams request via ticket and ops configures per request which delays onboarding and yields naming and permission drift. Goal: reduce manual steps, enforce org-level naming/permission guardrails, and auto-schedule archival while preserving auditability.
impact: Operational friction for onboarding new pods; repeated manual configuration errors (incorrect permissions, missing retention/archival tags); higher load on internal-support queue. Expected to reduce ticket volume for project setup by ~70% and onboarding time from days to minutes after rollout.
current_flow_steps: 1) Pod PM files ticket to internal-support with fields for project name and owners
2) Ops manually creates Jira project from template, Confluence space, and Slack channel
3) Ops copies onboarding checklist, assigns group roles and configures permission schemes
4) Manual archival reminder created in calendar or left to requestor
desired_flow_steps: 1) Requestor opens 'Create Project Bundle' form in internal portal
2) Form validates team, naming pattern, and required security options
3) Backend automation provisions Jira project from template, Confluence space from template, and Slack channel with enforced channel name and visibility
4) IAM groups and role assignments are applied automatically; audit log entry created; automated archival job scheduled at 180 days unless extended
policy_guardrails: Jira project key reserved naming and automatic role groups: <team>-dev, <team>-eng, <team>-ops
Confluence space template with pre-populated privacy classification and retention metadata
Require at least two project admins from different org units for high-risk classifications
security_considerations: Must integrate with SSO group mapping; ensure provisioned channels/spaces inherit DLP/retention labels. Any bootstrap flow must record an auditable event with initiator identity and consent checkbox for data classification. Work with Security to sign off on templates before pilot.
acceptance_criteria: One-click portal flow creates Jira project + Confluence space + Slack channel in test org without manual intervention
Provisioned artifacts inherit required permission groups and metadata tags
Audit log entries appear in central logging with user, timestamp, and artifact IDs
Admin override path exists for edge-cases and records justification
investigation_notes: Spun up a PoC using existing Jira project template ID 712-old-template; discovered template uses legacy permission scheme that lacks 'viewers' group — needs update

Slack provisioning API token scope requires admin.conversations:write and users:read; proposed to use a bot with workspace-admin consent scoped to a single org workspace rather than global admin token
Confluence template requires X-Page-Template header; automation library currently lacks upsert endpoint; need to add to ops-tooling
risks: Slack bot token scope could be over-privileged if not narrowly scoped
Automated archival might remove active but low-traffic projects if owners forget to extend
Race conditions when multiple requests try to create similar project keys simultaneously
